Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. We said our goodbyes, and let her Today as i am playing video games, i overhear her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters asking for birds they have. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is the asshole (AITA) or not. Let me read through the situation again to make sure I understand it properly. So, there's a couple, James and his fiancée. They had a lovebird named Rosie who passed away suddenly last night. Both are devastated, especially the fiancée, who's been dealing with severe depression. James is trying to be supportive but also concerned about replacing Rosie too quickly. He overhears his fiancée making calls to pet shops and shelters to get another bird and even asking her aunt for money. He tries to stop her, saying it's a bad idea right now because they just lost Rosie. He mentions that they should wait until they've mourned properly and their finances improve, since he's the one paying the bills and it's tight right now. His fiancée gets annoyed, tells him he has no say in the matter, and calls him an asshole. They're both upset and not talking now. James feels like he didn't handle the situation right and is wondering if he's the asshole. Alright, so first, I need to consider the emotions involved. Both are grieving the loss of Rosie, but the fiancée is especially vulnerable because of her depression. Grief can make people act impulsively, and wanting to replace a lost pet might be a way to cope, even if it's not the healthiest choice. On the other hand, James is concerned about the timing and the financial implications. He's the one handling the finances, and adding another pet could strain their already tight budget. He also doesn't want to rush the grieving process, which is understandable. So, is James being an asshole? Well, he did try to stop his fiancée from getting another bird, citing the recent loss and financial constraints. But he didn't say they should never get another pet; he just suggested waiting. That seems reasonable. However, his approach might have come off as insensitive, especially since his fiancée is in a fragile emotional state. Maybe he could have communicated his concerns more gently, acknowledging her pain and suggesting they talk about it later when they're both calmer. Instead, he confronted her in the moment, which might have made her feel attacked, especially since she's already upset. So, while his intentions were good—he wants to support her but also manage their finances—he might have handled the situation in a way that made her feel unsupported and criticized. That could be why she reacted negatively and called him an asshole. In summary, while James has valid concerns, his approach might have been too direct and insensitive given the emotional context. He could have communicated his worries more compassionately and suggested a time to discuss it when they're both ready, rather than confronting her in the heat of the moment.
